summary.headline: Zelio FY26 consolidated revenue rose 81.8% to INR313 crore, EBITDA INR38.01 crore at 12.2% margin, PAT INR28.39 crore; FY27 target 125,000 units.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) consolidated revenue from operations of INR310.71 crore (total revenue INR313.68 crore), up 81.8%, with EBITDA of INR38.01 crore and PAT of INR28.39 crore. Two-wheeler volumes reached more than 70,000 units (H1 30,000, H2 40,000+), and capacity was expanded from 72,000 to 240,000 units across four plants. Management guided to 75-80% revenue growth and more than 125,000 units in FY27, with Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu) and Patan (Haryana, three-wheelers) commissioned in July 2026 per the script. The call was largely Q&A on volumes, dealers, financing, capex and governance; many answers were qualitative or repeated the same targets.

segments.name: Two-wheelers (low-speed EV scooters)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume above 70,000 units, with H2 above H1 (40,000+ vs 30,000). Average selling price cited at about INR44,000, with management expecting INR45,000-50,000 over time.

segments.name: Three-wheelers
segments.commentary: FY26 volume of only 800 units because plant was not ready. FY27 target is more than 2,000 units, with production from the Patan, Haryana plant.

segments.name: Zelio Auto Components (wholly-owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Incorporated to control component procurement and spare parts supply; management says it is already contributing positively to consolidated revenue and profitability. No separate figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of more than 125,000 units.
Revenue growth target of 75-80% YoY, described as a repeatable structural trajectory.
Dealer network to expand from more than 400 to more than 550 in FY27 (100-150 new dealers); 100% of dealerships to be exclusive by this year.
Three-wheeler FY27 target of more than 2,000 units.

Management said EBITDA and PAT margins will be maintained despite higher branding and promotion spend; marketing spend for FY27 not yet decided, with FY26 non-IPL promotional spend stated as more than INR1 crore.
Five to six vehicles to be 70-80% Make in India by 2027; components to be 100% indigenous in-house by this year or next financial year (per management).
Management said the company will move to quarterly reporting in the future, but not immediately; it is currently required to report half-yearly.
capex_capacity: Capacity expanded from 72,000 to 240,000 units per annum in FY26 across four plants.
Ladwa, Haryana flagship: 120,000 units per annum; serves North and West India.
Cuttack, Odisha: 60,000 units per annum, operational and GST-registered since December 2025; gateway to East and Northeast India.
Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu: about 60,000 units per annum, commissioned in July 2026 per the script (an answer said operational from next month); Tamil Nadu GST active.
Patan, Haryana: electric three-wheeler and two-wheeler chassis plant, commissioned in July 2026 per the script. Three-wheeler fabrication to be in-house after this plant starts.
Management said IPO proceeds funded plant and machinery, mainly for the three-wheeler segment; capital advances for new plant and machinery were about INR25 lakh.
demand_pricing: Management cited a low-speed EV segment of 8-10 lakh units per year (about 40-45% of EV two-wheeler volumes), growing 20-25% per annum, priced INR50,000-75,000 with no licence or registration needed.
Management said crude price increases and government encouragement are driving switching to EVs; expects market growth of 20-25%.
Management targets more than 10% share of the EV market this year and 20-30% within 2-3 years; an analyst's calculation implied roughly 10-11% share on 125,000 units against 11-12 lakh market.
Financing: management cited tie-ups with Bajaj, Kotak and Trusera Finance; said finance options are available in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities.
Management said competition would not force price cuts; South India price list is expected to fall as Coimbatore transport costs decline.
Management said the monsoon has no effect on two-wheeler sales (IP67 motors and controllers); agricultural impact is said to delay, not reduce, sales.
Management expects 'no government support' for low-speed EVs currently beyond encouragement and registration/licence exemptions.

qa_highlights.question: Will a bad monsoon affect rural and Tier 2/3 demand, and how is consumer financing structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon does not hit sales (delays only) and cited tie-ups with Bajaj, Kotak and Trusera Finance for customer loans in Tier 1 and 2 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of INR43 crore loans and advances on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shubham Garg said supplier advances were about INR22.5 crore, capital advances INR25 lakh, and GST and customs refund claims INR19 crore, totalling about INR42.6 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate and how long does it last?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company has applied under Section 115BAB and pays 17% tax, which runs for 10 years from 2021, leaving about five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the Coimbatore plant produce and how does competition affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Coimbatore has about 60,000 units capacity, matching Odisha, and that lower transport costs will reduce South India prices without hurting EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin plans given higher branding spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it intends to keep profitability and margins similar while doubling or tripling volume, and that branding spend will not dent EBITDA or PAT growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is a bike segment planned, and how are three-wheeler service and spares handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no bike plans until battery costs fall; service engineers grew from four to more than 10, and the subsidiary handles spares.

risks_watch: Management's 75-80% growth and 125,000-unit targets rely on four plants and 550+ dealers being operational; the Coimbatore and Patan commissioning dates are stated in July 2026, after the period end.
Dependence on imported components (cells, from China and elsewhere) for parts not yet indigenised; management guided 70-80% Make in India by 2027.
Margin sustainability: management said EBITDA margin will hold despite higher promotion spend (IPL costs partly deferred as prepaid), and marketing spend for FY27 is undecided.
Three-wheeler volume was only 800 units in FY26, so the 2,000-unit FY27 target is an early-stage ramp.
Tax benefit under Section 115BAB runs about five more years; afterwards the tax rate is a risk.
Analyst concerns on the stock's periodic call auction; the company said it would write to SEBI and asked the broker to do the same.
Management did not explicitly break out segment-level profit or the subsidiary's contribution.
summary.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional, with repeated claims of 'truth' and 'no losses'. Management was specific on volumes, plants and dealer counts, but answers on margins, subsidies, FY27 marketing budget and quarterly reporting were vague or deferred.
key_quotes: And I want every investor on this call to hear this clearly : not a single quarter of losses.
I am committed to sustaining 75% to 80% year-on-year revenue growth as our structural trajectory.
However much we expand, however much budget we keep, our focus is to keep profitability and margins similar.
We are targeting more than 125,000 units scale for this year.

financial_highlights.change: Margin described as expanding; an analyst cited 11% margin for the year
